Matchbook Learning Morning Meeting · K–2 Behavior Toolkit · My Feelings07

Slide 1 · Title & Promise R2

Point to your own face and make a big smile, then a sad face. “Our faces and bodies tell us how we feel. Every feeling has a name. Today we learn to say how we feel.” Say together: “Every feeling has a name.”

Look for

  • Eyes on the slide or on you
  • Students copy your faces
  • Students repeat “Every feeling has a name”

If it breaks

  • If faces get silly: “Show me a happy face. Now a calm face.” End on calm, then move on.

Support adult

  • Sit near any student who has had a hard morning; never ask a student to share a feeling they did not choose to share

Language support

  • Feeling words are new for many students: say each one with a matching face
  • Spanish: sentimientos · Kreyòl: santiman

Engagement move Equity stick: pull one name and ask, “Show me a happy face.” Any happy face is a full answer.

All feelings are okay. Feelings are not good or bad; some feel good and some feel hard. Say it that way every time.

Slide 2 · Regulate · Get Calm First R1

Model the gesture with them every time. “Smell the flower. Blow out the candle. Long and slow. Three times.” Do it with the class, not from the front.

Look for

  • Exhale longer than inhale
  • Shoulders drop
  • Gesture copied

If it breaks

  • If silliness: model silently once, then invite them back.

Support adult

  • Breathe audibly beside any student who cannot settle

Language support

  • No language demand; gesture carries it
  • Same two gestures used in every K–2 lesson

Engagement move LiveSchool: award a point to a student who breathes all three times with you. Name the behavior: “You breathed slow three times.”

Ask: “How does your body feel now?” One or two quick answers. This is the first naming practice of the day.

Slide 3 · Orient · The Story R2, R3

Point to each picture as you tell it. “It was Lee’s turn to read out loud. Her tummy felt funny and her hands felt shaky. She noticed her body. She named her feeling: ‘I feel worried.’ She told her teacher. Her teacher said, ‘Thank you for telling me. Let’s read together.’ Lee read, and she felt proud.” Then have the class say together: “I notice my body. I name my feeling.”

Look for

  • Students follow the pictures in order
  • Whole class repeats the We say line

If it breaks

  • If students say Lee is a baby for being worried: “Everyone feels worried sometimes. Even grown-ups. Lee was brave to say it.”

Support adult

  • Point to each panel as the teacher narrates

Language support

  • Four pictures, two words each; numbers carry the order
  • Act out “tummy feels funny” by rubbing your tummy

Engagement move Equity stick: “Which picture shows Lee naming her feeling? Point.” Pointing is a full answer.

Naming a feeling makes it smaller. Lee did not have to hide it or act it out; she said it.

Slide 4 · Connect · Turn and Talk R3, R4

Show knee to knee with a student partner. “Turn knee to knee. Look at Lee’s face and body. Tell your partner: Lee feels ___.” Give 30 seconds, then ring back. Ask one pair: “How did you know?”

Look for

  • Partners face each other
  • Students name worried or point to the worried face
  • Some students name a body clue

If it breaks

  • If a pair is stuck: kneel in and say the stem with them.
  • If partners argue: “Take turns. You go first, then you.”

Support adult

  • Pair any student who needs support with a steady partner before the lesson starts

Language support

  • Pointing to a face is a complete answer
  • Spanish: “Siente preocupación” · Kreyòl: “Li santi l enkyete”

Engagement move Equity stick: call two names to share. Praise the clue: “You saw her worried eyebrows. Great noticing!”

Slide 5 · Practice · Watch Me, Then Show Me R3, R4, R5

Read the scene. “My friend gives me a high five. I feel…” Invite one student to show the face and say the sentence: “I feel happy.” Ask the class, “What clue did you see?” Then read two more: “My tower falls down.” “It is my turn to read out loud.” A new student models each one. Then the whole class shows each face together.

Look for

  • A student shows a face and says “I feel ___.”
  • Class names the clue they saw
  • Whole class practices all four faces

If it breaks

  • Excellent model: “Show the class again. Everyone, what feeling was that?”
  • Partly right model: “You showed the face. Now say the sentence: I feel ___.”
  • Silly model: “Thank you. Let’s see it the calm way.” Call a new student; no commentary.

Support adult

  • Hold up the four face cards so students can point instead of naming

Language support

  • Four faces with words; students can point instead of naming
  • Model “I feel ___.” as a sentence everyone says
  • Spanish: “Siento ___.” · Kreyòl: “Mwen santi m ___.”

Engagement move LiveSchool: award the student model a point for using the full sentence. Name it out loud.

Students model, not the teacher. Accept any feeling a student can explain; there is no single right answer for “My tower falls down.”

Slide 6 · Commit · My Promise Today R2, R5

Put your hand on your heart. “Say it with me: I can name my feeling.” Then: “Point to how you feel right now.” Model it first: “Right now, I feel happy.”

Look for

  • Every student says the promise
  • Every student points to one face

If it breaks

  • If a student does not choose: offer two faces and let them point.
  • Never push a student to explain a hard feeling in front of the class.

Support adult

  • Check in quietly later with any student who points to sad, mad, or worried

Language support

  • Hand on heart carries the promise
  • Spanish: Puedo decir lo que siento · Kreyòl: Mwen ka di sa m santi

Engagement move Equity stick: pull three names: “Which face did you point to?” Pointing counts.

A student who points to sad, mad, or worried gets a quiet check-in after the meeting, not a public conversation.

Slide 7 · Transition · How We Leave R1, R4, R5

“How we leave is how we start our learning. Stand up. Calm face. Walk. Ready to learn. Let’s practice.” Do not time this at K–2.

Look for

  • Calm faces and bodies while moving
  • Calm walking, not rushing

If it breaks

  • “Let’s try that again. Back to your spot.” Rebuild clean, no commentary on individuals.

Support adult

  • Stand at the destination, not behind the group

Language support

  • Four icons, four words
  • No timing pressure at this age

Engagement move LiveSchool: award a point to the table that walks with calm bodies the whole way.

Name feelings out loud all day: “You look excited. You look frustrated.” Students learn the words by hearing them.
